'''Jamal Wesley Sampson''' (born May 15, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] before being selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round (47th overall) of the [[2002 NBA draft]].

==College career==
Sampson played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] in 2001–02, where he averaged 6.4 points, 6.5 rebounds and 1.17 blocks in 32 games. He posted four double-doubles, and had 15 points, 17 rebounds and four blocks versus [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. He was named to the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-10]] All-Freshman Team.<ref name=raptors08>{{cite news |title=Raptors Sign Jamal Sampson |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/jamalsampson_pressrelease.html |access-date=13 September 2025 |work=NBA.com |date=30 September 2008}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Sampson was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round (47th overall) of the [[2002 NBA draft]]. He was immediately traded by the Jazz to the [[Orlando Magic]], and then again by the Magic to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on draft night.<ref name=nuggets06>{{cite news |title=Nuggets Sign Sampson |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets_sign_sampson_072806.html |access-date=13 September 2025 |work=NBA.com |date=28 July 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070516023028/http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets_sign_sampson_072806.html |archive-date=16 May 2007}}</ref> He signed with the Bucks on September 30, 2002, but was waived on July 10, 2003, after one season.<ref name=realgm>{{cite web |title=Jamal Sampson Player Profile, Boston Celtics - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jamal-Sampson/Summary/501 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=12 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

On July 24, 2003, Sampson signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref name="realgm" /> After playing 10 games for the Lakers in 2003–04, he was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in the [[2004 NBA Expansion Draft|expansion draft]] in June 2004.<ref name="realgm" /> He was waived by the Bobcats on February 8, 2005.<ref name="realgm" /> He posted career-best averages of 3.4 points and 5.3 rebounds in 23 games for Charlotte in the 2004–05 season.<ref name="raptors08" />

On August 8, 2005, Sampson signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref name="realgm" /> He appeared in 12 games for the Kings during the 2005–06 season.<ref name="nuggets06" />

On July 28, 2006, Sampson signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref name="nuggets06" /> He played 22 games in 2006–07, with his final NBA game coming on April 18, 2007, in a 100–77 victory over the [[San Antonio Spurs]], where Sampson recorded 13 rebounds in 27 minutes as a starter.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jamal Sampson 2006-07 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/sampsja01/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=12 September 2025 |work=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On October 1, 2007, Sampson signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref name="realgm" /> He was waived on October 22, prior to the start of the regular season.<ref name="realgm" />

In November 2007, Sampson had an unsuccessful tryout with German team [[Skyliners Frankfurt]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Freche Franzosen klauen die Punkte in den letzten Sekunden |url=https://www.frankfurt-skyliners.de/news-service/details/freche-franzosen-klauen-die-punkte-in-den-letzten-sekunden |access-date=12 September 2025 |work=www.frankfurt-skyliners.de |date=27 November 2007 |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Links |url=https://www.frankfurt-skyliners.de/news-service/details/links-91 |access-date=12 September 2025 |work=www.frankfurt-skyliners.de |date=30 November 2007 |language=de-DE}}</ref> In December 2007, he signed with [[Liaoning Flying Leopards|Liaoning Panpan Hunters]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA) for the rest of the season.<ref name=shamsports>{{cite web |title=Jamal Sampson Player Profile |url=https://www.shamsports.com/player-profile?pid=344 |website=shamsports.com |access-date=12 September 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250912130929/https://www.shamsports.com/player-profile?pid=344 |archive-date=12 September 2025}}</ref> In April 2008, he signed with [[Zain Club|Zain]] of the [[Jordanian Premier Basketball League]] for the rest of the season.<ref name="shamsports" />

On September 30, 2008, Sampson signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref name="raptors08" /> He was waived on October 22, prior to the start of the regular season.<ref name="realgm" /> Two days later, he signed with [[Shenzhen Leopards|DongGuan New Century]] for the 2008–09 CBA season.<ref name="shamsports" /> He left DongGuan in February 2009.<ref name="shamsports" />

In December 2009, Sampson signed with [[Smart Gilas]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) during the [[2009–10 PBA season|2009–10 season]].<ref name="shamsports" /> He replaced [[C. J. Giles]] as the team's candidate to be a naturalized player for future international competitions.<ref>[http://businessmirror.com.ph/home/sports/19370-sampson-signs-contract-with-smart-gilas.html Sampson signs contract with Smart Gilas] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100115174817/http://businessmirror.com.ph/home/sports/19370-sampson-signs-contract-with-smart-gilas.html |date=January 15, 2010 }} - Business Mirror, 6 December 2009 21:36</ref> Sampson left Smart Gilas in January 2010.<ref name="shamsports" />

In November 2010, Sampson joined [[Shanxi Loongs|Shanxi Brave Dragons]] for the 2010–11 CBA season.<ref name="shamsports" /><ref>{{cite web|author=Jon Pastuszek |url=http://www.niubball.com/2010/12/fujian-to-release-patrick-obryant-shanxi-adds-jamal-sampson/ |title=Fujian to release Patrick O'Bryant, Shanxi adds Jamal Sampson |publisher=Niubball.com |date=December 8, 2010 |access-date=December 23, 2011}}</ref> He left the team in December 2010.<ref name="shamsports" />

In November 2011, Sampson was selected by the [[Texas Legends]] with the fifth overall pick in the [[2011 NBA Development League draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2011/index.html |title=2011 NBA D-League Draft |work=NBA.com |access-date=December 23, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111207031237/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2011/index.html |archive-date=December 7, 2011 }}</ref> He appeared in two games for the Legends to start the [[2011–12 NBA Development League season|2011–12 NBA D-League season]]<ref name="realgm" /> before signing with the [[Boston Celtics]] on December 12 for training camp.<ref name="realgm" /><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060226094519/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 26, 2006|title=Celtics invite 4 to training camp|last=Washburn|first=Gary|date=December 8, 2011|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|access-date=December 9, 2011}}</ref> He was waived by the Celtics on December 22, prior to the start of the [[2011–12 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press122211-celtics-waive-sampson.html |title=Celtics Waive Sampson |work=NBA.com |date=December 22, 2011 |access-date=December 23, 2011}}</ref> He was waived by the Legends on January 9, 2012.<ref name="realgm" />

==Personal life==
Sampson is the cousin of former NBA All-Star, [[Ralph Sampson]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jamal_sampson/bio.html Jamal Sampson] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070116182427/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jamal_sampson/bio.html |date=January 16, 2007 }} at NBA.com</ref>
